text:
maria_suarez: Customer (large GCP consumer) requested a practical playbook for Interconnect + Private Service Connect connectivity to Redwood Private. They want explicit steps for egress allowlist, DNS handling, MTU guidance, BGP snippet, and firewall rules.

ajackson: Do they prefer PSC or VPC peering for the POC?

maria_suarez: They prefer PSC for managed endpoints, but security wants a peering fallback if PSCterminates client IPs. They also want guidance for preserving client source IPs for audit logs.

tyler_ops: Short answer: PSC terminates the connection so source IP will be our connector IP unless you use a path that preserves client IPs (e.g., VPC peering or run the runtime inside their VPC). For PSC + preserve-IP semantics you can proxy and inject PROXY protocol from their edge, or request a NAT-less route to our VPC (rare).

nora_net: Draft egress CIDR for them to allow during POC: `35.199.128.0/18` and `34.72.0.0/16` (placeholder; will provide exact pinned pool once requested).

maria_suarez: MTU question: embeddings payloads sometimes have large TCP segments. Interconnect adds VLAN encapsulation; what's the recommendation?

tyler_ops: Recommend an end-to-end MTU of 1460. Customers should clamp MSS on on-prem firewalls and set tunnel MTU to 1460 to avoid fragmentation. Add note: verify with `ping -M do -s` tests.

nora_net: Pasteable firewall examples for their net team:

```
# Allow outbound HTTPS to Redwood egress pool (example IPs)
allow tcp from 10.10.0.0/16 to 35.199.128.0/18 ports 443
allow icmp from 10.10.0.0/16 to 35.199.128.0/18 (for MTU/diagnostics)
# BGP and interconnect prep (allow BGP TCP 179 if using BGP sessions)
allow tcp from their-bgp-peer-ip to our-peer-ip ports 179
```

ajackson: Also remind them to assign `roles/compute.networkUser` to the PSC consumer service account and to add the consumer attachment in their project.

maria_suarez: Security questionnaire Q: "Can Redwood run inside our VPC?" Answer: Yes. Options: 1) Redwood-hosted via PSC/peering with egress allowlist, 2) Dedicated/Private deployment inside customer VPC or on-prem (we provide an appliance/container), 3) Hybrid (control plane outside, runtime in their VPC). We'll outline tradeoffs (auditability, latency, egress billing).

infra_bot: [automated] Attachments: tentative-egress-list.csv, psc-arch-diagram-v2.png

tyler_ops: Pricing note for sales: call out GCP Interconnect egress bandwidth charges and potential cross-connect circuit fees. For Reserved Dedicated capacity we can include a committed throughput line item to smooth unit cost; mention that egress pools can be pinned for POC at no extra infra charge.

maria_suarez: Failover strategy they asked for: multi-region Interconnect + PSC primary, peering fallback in another region. We'll recommend healthcheck + BGP community priority to shift.

nora_net: Healthcheck guidance: 3 probes, 10s interval, fail after 3 misses. Use TCP/443 to our per-account health path `/hc/rls` (tokenized).

ajackson: Action items: nora_net to deliver firewall + BGP + MTU checklist (EOD tomorrow); tyler_ops to write pricing blurb for Interconnect + reserved capacity; maria_suarez to assemble playbook and Q&A.

sales_ops: Customer wants POC in 2 weeks. Can we commit?

tyler_ops: Feasible if we pin an egress pool and pre-create PSC endpoint. Need BGP creds and point of contact from their network team within 3 business days.

nora_net: Sample BGP snippet for their engineers to copy:

```
neighbor 203.0.113.21 remote-as 64512
neighbor 203.0.113.21 description redwood-interconnect-peer
network 10.20.0.0/20
```

maria_suarez: I'll draft the outbound email with playbook attached and request their network contact and timeline. Who can review before I send?

ajackson: I'll check the PSC IAM sections.

tyler_ops: I'll review pricing and timing.

infra_bot: [automated] Draft uploaded to /shared/sales/poc-playbooks/4812345678-poc-playbook-draft.pdf

maria_suarez: Thanks all, sending tomorrow unless anyone objects. :thumbsup:
